dct_description_sm: Over the last decade, the changes to local weather patterns and climate have seen a reduction in the period when winter roads may be opened for safe travel. Cat Lake recently experienced four years where a winter road was not able to be opened. This resulted in excessive shipping costs. By rerouting the Cat Lake First Nation winter road, the community would see the following benefits and opportunities: (1) longer, more reliable and safer access to the community for people, goods/materials and fuel; (2) reduced shipping costs to the community; (3) reduced travel time; (4) shared winter road operation & maintenance costs with neighbouring First Nations; (5) potential opportunities for economic development; and (6) opportunities for skill/knowledge transfer to the First Nation during design/construction of the new road.
